justification_text:
The point estimates at each time horizon reflect my best estimate of the likely value of the forecasted variable at that time. In this case, I expect relatively small changes over the short term (1 day) due to the general stability of the underlying trends or dynamics driving the forecast. Over the medium term (1 week and 1 month), the point estimates adjust slightly upward, likely reflecting either an anticipated trend of gradual growth or reversion to some longer-term mean. These estimates incorporate the best available data and assume no major disruptions, using both historical patterns and any known short-term factors that could influence outcomes.

The confidence intervals widen as the forecast period lengthens because uncertainty increases over time. In the short term (the 1-day interval), the range is very narrow, reflecting high confidence due to minimal time for unexpected events or deviations. Over 1 week and especially over 1 month, more variables come into play, creating broader confidence intervals. Uncertainty sources may include unforeseen shifts in relevant trends, external shocks (such as market, political, or environmental disruptions), or underlying volatility in the system being forecasted. These factors collectively contribute to the greater spread of possible outcomes further into the future.

Specific risks or events could push outcomes outside the stated confidence intervals, particularly over the longer horizons. For example, if this forecast relates to a financial market variable, an unexpected economic report, policy announcement, or geopolitical event could cause significant deviations. If it pertains to something like weather, extreme or anomalous conditions might also lie outside the modeled uncertainty bounds. The ability of the forecast to account for such risks is limited, as these are often rare or difficult to predict in advance. This is why the confidence intervals, especially for the 1-week and 1-month horizons, can only capture typical uncertainty, not extreme outlier events.
